scope.primary_use: Flat lithophanes, night-light stands, and globe lithophanes
scope.principle: Lithophanes use varying thickness to control transmitted light: thin areas appear bright and thick areas appear dark.
scope.validation: Print a small test lithophane with the intended backlight before producing a final stand or globe.

pla_white.notes: White PLA is the recommended baseline for a classic black-and-white lithophane; use a cool-white backlight.

pla_colored_or_dark.notes: Darker or colored filament transmits less light; community reports indicate dark areas may need roughly 3.6 mm to render properly. Treat 3.6 mm as a starting upper bound, not a universal rule.

petg.notes: PETG can be used, but PLA is more commonly recommended for visual quality. Start with the PLA range and increase maximum thickness only after a backlight test.

general_rules: Use 100% infill or a solid lithophane body so thickness variations control light transmission.
Print the lithophane vertically for best detail and layer consistency.
Use a 0.4 mm nozzle and a layer height around 0.12 mm as a practical starting point.
Use a cool-white backlight for conventional monochrome lithophanes.
Avoid clear filament as the default: white PLA generally gives stronger contrast for classic lithophanes.

led_puck.typical_use: Flat lithophane frames and small night lights
led_puck.design_rule: Size the recess to the measured puck diameter plus clearance; do not assume a universal puck size.
led_puck.notes: A 156 mm x 120 mm USB-C powered backlight board is one documented example for larger color lithophanes.

tea_light.design_rule: Measure the actual tea-light diameter and height; provide ventilation and a removable battery/LED carrier.
tea_light.caution: Do not enclose a flame-based tea light in plastic; use LED tea lights for 3D-printed stands.

e12_bulb.typical_use: Small decorative bulbs and night lights
e12_bulb.notes: E12 refers to a 12 mm screw-base diameter; add clearance for the socket, wiring, heat, and insertion.

e26_bulb.notes: E26 refers to a 26 mm screw-base diameter; use a lamp socket or certified fixture rather than modeling a mains-voltage socket as a casual 3D-printed part.

safety: Prefer low-heat LED sources over incandescent or flame sources.
Do not enclose flame-based candles in PLA or PETG.
For mains-voltage bulbs, use a certified socket, cord, and assembly; do not treat a printed socket as an electrical component.
Provide ventilation around LED electronics and avoid sealing battery compartments without access.

globe_lithophanes.approach: Parameterize the globe from the selected light source and printer build volume; do not use one fixed globe diameter as a universal standard.

small_desk_globe.light_source: LED puck or E12 LED bulb

medium_globe.light_source: LED puck or E26 LED bulb

opening_rules: Size the opening from the actual light-source diameter plus at least 0.6 mm total clearance.
For an E12 LED bulb, begin with a 12.6 mm opening; for E26, begin with a 26.6 mm opening.
For an LED puck, use puck diameter plus 0.3 mm minimum radial clearance.
Keep an access opening large enough to install and remove the light source and wiring.
Add a mounting lip, threaded cap, or friction-fit collar only after measuring the actual hardware.
print_notes: Split large globes into hemispheres or vertical panels if they exceed the build volume.
Print lithophane panels vertically and join them with aligned tabs, dovetails, or adhesive-friendly flanges.
Avoid supports inside the image area; orient seams away from the most detailed facial or image regions.

cmyk_lithophanes.method: Use four separate lithophane layers printed in cyan, magenta, yellow, and black filament, then stack and align them.
design_rules: Generate each CMYK channel as its own height map or lithophane layer.
Maintain consistent XY registration across all four layers; misalignment produces color fringing.
Use white or light-colored backing/light diffusion where the method calls for it.
Print each color layer with the same orientation and scaling to preserve alignment.
Use a bright, diffuse backlight; color lithophanes need more transmitted light than monochrome lithophanes.
Start with a small CMYK test image before committing to a large globe or panel.
cmyk_lithophanes.sources_note: Bambu Lab and Snapmaker document CMYK color lithophanes as stacked color layers, with Bambu recommending a 0.15 mm first layer and Snapmaker documenting a 156 mm x 120 mm USB-C backlight board.
